validity.recommendation: Row is a real pipeline and is not a duplicate.
validity.researcher_notes: The Gazprom page describes Ukhta-Torzhok as a 2011 to 2012 build of about 970 km, 1420 mm and 45 billion cubic meters per year, together with its twin Ukhta-Torzhok 2. The older 1960s Ukhta-Torzhok trunk is a different line. A February 2023 Upstream report of ruptures concerns Ukhta-Torzhok 3, which is also a different line.

fills.researcher_notes: Status operating is confirmed. A Gazprom project page, kept by the Wayback Machine in November 2022, says Ukhta-Torzhok was built from 2011 and put into operation in 2012. The Gazprom annual report for 2022 lists the new Ukhta-Torzhok pipeline as the continuation of the northern corridor after Bovanenkovo-Ukhta. Both pages come from Gazprom, so they are not counted as independent.

Operator Gazprom Transgaz Ukhta is supported at medium. A 2018 news item says the Gryazovets compressor station branch of Gazprom Transgaz Ukhta runs the lines that start at that station, and Ukhta-Torzhok is on the list. The item does not say the company runs this line by itself, and the page is about the whole station.

status_reviews.staleness_rule: Annual update. A dated Gazprom page from November 2022 shows the line built and in operation, and no stop or change was found.
status_reviews.researcher_notes: Status operating is kept. The harvested citations show the line in operation since 2012 and show no shutdown.
